patch_description: The current function returns all zeros, giving a min area of 0. I propose a two-stage deterministic constructor: (1) initialize with a hand-designed, symmetric configuration known to be strong for the Heilbronn problem in an equilateral triangle (vertices + edge midpoints + a coarse interior lattice, which spreads points evenly and avoids tiny-area triplets), and (2) refine it with a deterministic, seeded coordinate-descent hill climb that maximizes the minimum triangle area over all C(11,3)=165 triplets, while keeping every point inside the triangle via half-plane constraints. The min-area is computed vectorized for speed, and the whole refinement is bounded in iterations so eval_time stays modest. Determinism is guaranteed with a fixed RNG seed; failure of the optimizer cannot make things worse since perturbations are only accepted when they strictly improve the objective.
